image.shortdescription: Two vectors and a set of skewed grid lines representing their linear combinations.

description.p: There is a set of coordinate axes and a standard 1\times1 coordinate grid in the background. There are also two vectors \vvec_1=\twovec21 and \vvec_2=\twovec12 and two sets of parallel lines representing the linear combinations of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2. One set of parallel lines is parallel to \vvec_1 and passes through the integer multiples of \vvec_2 while the other set is parallel to \vvec_2 and passes through integer multiples of \vvec_1.

statement.p: Indicate the linear combination \vvec_1 - 2\vvec_2 on the figure.

solution.p: We can see graphically, or we can compute, that \vvec_1-2\vvec_2 = \twovec{0}{-3}.

statement.p: Express the vector \twovec{-3}{0} as a linear combination of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2.

solution.p: Since the linear combination extends beyond the figure, we compute that 10\vvec_1-13\vvec_2 = \twovec{7}{-16}.

statement.p: Express the vector \twovec{16}{-4} as a linear combination of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2.

solution.p: We need to find the solution to the linear system c_1\vvec_1 + c_2\vvec_2 = \twovec{16}{-4}, which is \twovec{c_1}{c_2} = \twovec{12}{-8}.

statement.p: Explain why every vector in \real^2 can be written as a linear combination of \vvec_1 and \vvec_2 in exactly one way.

solution.p: The matrix \left[\begin{array}{rr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \end{array}\right] has a pivot position in every row and every column.
